course_description:
Design, build, and test a mechanical system that fulfills a set of requirements and performance criteria. Work in a team to execute the project within time and budgetary constraints. Use digital tools (CAD, FEM, PLM), disciplinary knowledge, and design standards/practices to develop solutions that are manufacturable, functional, and safe.

The conceptualisation, design, validation, and operation of complex systems that efficiently and reliably perform their intended function are core to the engineering profession. This course is a capstone course in the ‘Design Stream’ of your curriculum and marks an important milestone in your journey of becoming a professional engineer.

ENGG1100 introduced you to the discipline of professional engineering and its principal fields. MECH2305 followed with an introduction to Engineering Design and Manufacturing. In MECH2100, you learned how to design key machine elements such as bolted connections, gears, and bearings. MECH3610 introduced you to the key concepts of systems engineering and principles of project management. In addition to the ‘Design Stream’ courses, you have also acquired a wealth of foundational knowledge through the other courses in the curriculum. This course will be your first opportunity to put all these learnings to practical use, cement previous learnings, and expand your discipline-specific understanding of systems engineering.

In this course, you are expected to work in teams using systems engineering principles to design, evaluate, build, assemble and test a substantive mechanical system. You will demonstrate the practice of mechanical system design as part of a project team. The course environment simulates the challenges facing a small manufacturing company designing a product for a competitive marketplace.

course_aims: MECH3100 develops systems thinking and practical design capability through a team based mechanical system design project. Students apply structured design methods, CAD/FEA tools, and PLM workflows. The course emphasises requirement-driven design, digital collaboration, technical communication, hands-on fabrication, and risk management.

learning_outcomes.description: Mitigate project risks by communicating progress, contributing equitably, meeting milestones, and maintaining accountability throughout the duration of a team-based mechanical design project.

Generate, evaluate, and select design solutions that meet prescribed system requirements using structured approaches, such as morphological analysis, concept scoring matrices, and design for manufacturability principles.

Identify and apply regulations, engineering standards, and industry codes pertaining to safety, design documentation, and design practice throughout the detailed implementation of the mechanical system design.

Integrate sustainability principles into design decisions by selecting low environmental-impact materials, designing for maintenance and disassembly, and selecting manufacturing processes that balance performance, cost, and resource efficiency.

Apply Computer Aided Design (CAD) tools to create parametric three-dimensional models of mechanical components and assemblies, and Finite Element Analysis (FEA) tools predict structural response to loads and optimise component geometry/assembly layout.

Apply Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) methods and tools throughout the system design process to manage design data, maintain version control, facilitate collaborative workflows, and ensure design traceability from requirements through to manufacturing documentation.

Build a functional system prototype using the facilities and safe working procedures of an engineering makerspace and perform verification and validation tests to confirm that the prototype meets design and safety requirements.

Effectively communicate design decisions, analysis results, verification and validation outcomes, and manufacturing documentation through technical reports, presentations, and technical drawings that meet industry standards for documentation and communication.

assessment_details.title: Performance Validation, Design Handover, and Disassembly
assessment_details.category: Paper/ Report/ Annotation, Performance, Product/ Design
assessment_details.due_date: Performance Validation - 20% Week 11 Mon - Week 13 Thu Design Handover - 30% Week 13 Fri - Week 13 Fri Disassembly Workshop - 5% Exam week 1 Mon - Exam week 2 Fri
assessment_details.other_conditions: Peer assessed, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Performance Validation - 20% Teams will collaborate in the engineering makerspace and laboratory space to fabricate and test a physical prototype of their mechanical system design. The teams will verify that the prototype meets the system requirements. The teams will validate the system performance against the prescribed targets. Teams will receive multiple supervised testing opportunities from Week 11 to Week 13 and a testing schedule will be communicated via Blackboard. Design Handover - 30% Teams will hand over their prototype system to the teaching staff upon completion of performance testing in Week 13. Teams must hand over the system without modifying or removing any components that were part of the system during performance testing. Teams will also hand over up-to-date digital design data in the PLM environment (formal revision workflows in PLM to reflect any design changes made since the detailed design review assessment, up-to-date CAD replica of the physical prototype). Teams will also submit a formal report on Blackboard providing: (1) an as-built Manufacturing Bill of Materials that identifies the quantity, source, and cost of every component/part on the prototype, (2) tracing each UQ-fabricated part from the final product to its manufacturing drawing, source material, and fabrication process, (3) a complete and up to date engineering drawing package comprising of all assemblies, subassemblies, and components/parts (revised from the original drawing package submission from Assessment 3). An Excel spreadsheet for UQ card expenditure and receipts to also be uploaded on Blackboard as part of the same submission. Disassembly Workshop - 5% During the examination periods, teams will return to disassemble their prototype systems using basic hand tools. Disassembly workshop time and venue will be communicated to students after the release of the examination timetable. The teaching staff will assess the completeness of the disassembly and the reusability of the COTS parts and components. assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Submission requirements and marking rubric are provided on the course Blackboard site.
Deferral or extension
You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
Extensions are not possible for this assessment item as it is the final assessment of a semester-long design project and multiple assessment opportunities are provided during semester. This assessment cannot be deferred. Students who have valid grounds for an extension will receive the team mark.
Late submission
You will receive a mark of 0 if this assessment is submitted late .
Multiple testing opportunities are provided in Weeks 11 to 13 for the 'Performance Testing' component of this assessment sequence. The assessment concluded at the end of Week 13 and further testing during revision week or examination period is not permitted.
The 'Build Quality' and 'Disassembly Workshop' components run during scheduled times, with multiple markers arranged in advance. Hence, late submission (i.e., not arriving at the allocated time) is not permitted. This is consistent with industry practice around meetings with clients/industry partners. It is not necessary for all members of a team to be present for the latter assessment components. If none of the team members can attend their scheduled assessment time, contact the course coordinator to arrange an alternative time.

assessment_details.task_description: All students must formally meet with their mentor (an academic staff or delegated casual demonstrator) once a week during the weekly studio sessions. In these meetings, students must engage in discussion with their mentors and actively show evidence of progress towards assessment deliverables. The mentors will evaluate the degree of participation based on progress updates from students and the evidence of their individual progress presented in-person. assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Each student must provide a written progress statement to their team’s project coordinator on a weekly basis, following a prescribed format made available on Blackboard. The team’s project coordinator shall compile the statements and submit these to Blackboard prior to each studio session. The compiled progress update should explain how each student in a team participated adequately in the project work by progressing towards the assessment deliverables since the previous week’s discussion.
During the weekly studio sessions, their mentor (an academic staff or delegated casual demonstrator) will interview each student in person and evaluate the student’s participation based on their written progress update and evidence of progress provided in-person.
Deferral or extension
You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
There are ten (10) opportunities to fulfil this requirement throughout the semester, with students only required to participate in person and demonstrate satisfactory progress a minimum of five (5) times across the semester.
Late submission
You will receive a mark of 0 if this assessment is submitted late .
Consistent with industry practice, meetings are scheduled and time-bound, no late submissions will be accepted and a 100% late penalty applies.

Teaching staff and casual demonstrators will provide guidance on your design choices, project progress, and appropriate use of digital and physical tools and facilities. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L08

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13 (27 Jul - 01 Nov)

The workshops will mainly involve peer-based learning of effective strategies to perform the various design and coordination roles. Teaching staff and casual demonstrators will facilitate discussions and activities in several parallel streams, corresponding to the different defined roles. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L08
